text:
Research distinguishes recency dependence, replacement semantics, and joint positional effects. [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.09722) proposes measuring excessive emphasis on recent interactions; sensitivity alone does not establish that the emphasis is harmful. [ICMA](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.222.pdf) substitutes related items at existing positions, providing a useful precedent for perturbations that preserve sequence length and order. [Spotify’s benchmark study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling) compares last-item, independent pairwise-history, and Transformer models: earlier history can improve predictions without requiring joint interactions among history items.

Suggested diagnostic controls, synthesized from these distinctions: use the same donor item in paired recent-versus-older replacements; match replacement difficulty using training popularity and similarity to the displaced item. Preserve padding, sequence length, timestamps, and all untouched positions. Analyze final-position replacement separately; hold the final item fixed when comparing earlier positions, then cross donor identity with replacement position to expose content–position interactions. Keep each user’s candidate pool and eligibility mask identical across perturbations, so newly inserted or removed history items cannot change ranking eligibility. Measure donor score/rank changes separately from changes among other candidates, and repeat comparisons on a common pool excluding donor items to detect replacement-item self-recommendation. Report paired validation HR@10 changes and ranking stability across multiple donors, with uncertainty. These controls are proposed experimental design choices, not a standardized protocol established by the cited papers.
